an10.20:1.1: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Kurus, near the Kuru town named Kammāsadamma.
an10.20:1.2: There the Buddha addressed the bhikkhus:
an10.20:2.1: “There are these ten abodes of the noble ones in which the noble ones of the past, present, and future abide.
an10.20:2.3: A bhikkhu has given up five factors, possesses six factors, has a single guard, has four supports, has cast aside idiosyncratic interpretations of the truth, has totally given up searching, has unsullied intentions, has stilled the physical process, and is well freed in mind and well freed by wisdom.
an10.20:3.1: And how has a bhikkhu given up five factors?
an10.20:3.2: It’s when a bhikkhu has given up sensual desire, ill will, dullness and drowsiness, restlessness and remorse, and doubt.
an10.20:3.3: That’s how a bhikkhu has given up five factors.
an10.20:4.1: And how does a bhikkhu possess six factors?
an10.20:4.2: It’s when a bhikkhu, seeing a sight with their eyes, is neither happy nor sad. They remain equanimous, with awareness and comprehension.
an10.20:4.3: Hearing a sound with their ears …
an10.20:4.4: Smelling an odor with their nose …
an10.20:4.5: Tasting a flavor with their tongue …
an10.20:4.6: Feeling a touch with their body …
an10.20:4.7: Knowing an idea with their mind, they’re neither happy nor sad. They remain equanimous, with awareness and comprehension.
an10.20:4.8: That’s how a bhikkhu possesses six factors.
an10.20:5.1: And how does a bhikkhu have a single guard?
an10.20:5.2: It’s when a bhikkhu’s heart is guarded by mindfulness.
an10.20:5.3: That’s how a bhikkhu has a single guard.
an10.20:6.1: And how does a bhikkhu have four supports?
an10.20:6.2: After appraisal, a bhikkhu uses some things, endures some things, avoids some things, and gets rid of some things.
an10.20:6.3: That’s how a bhikkhu has four supports.
an10.20:7.1: And how has a bhikkhu cast aside idiosyncratic interpretations of the truth?
an10.20:7.2: Different ascetics and brahmins have different idiosyncratic interpretations of the truth. For example:
an10.20:7.3: the cosmos is eternal, or not eternal, or finite, or infinite; the soul and the body are one and the same, or the soul is one thing, the body another; after death, a realized one still exists, or no longer exists, or both still exists and no longer exists, or neither still exists nor no longer exists.
an10.20:7.4: A bhikkhu has cast out, cast aside, thrown out, discarded, let go of, given up, and relinquished all these.
an10.20:7.5: That’s how a bhikkhu has cast aside idiosyncratic interpretations of the truth.
an10.20:8.1: And how has a bhikkhu totally given up searching?
an10.20:8.2: It’s when they’ve given up searching for sensual pleasures, for continued existence, and for a spiritual life.
an10.20:8.3: That’s how a bhikkhu has totally given up searching.
an10.20:9.1: And how does a bhikkhu have unsullied intentions?
an10.20:9.2: It’s when a bhikkhu has given up intentions of sensuality, malice, and cruelty.
an10.20:9.3: That’s how a bhikkhu has unsullied intentions.
an10.20:10.1: And how has a bhikkhu stilled the physical process?
an10.20:10.2: It’s when, with the giving up of pleasure and pain and the disappearance of former happiness and sadness, they enter and dwell in the fourth stage of meditation, without pleasure or pain, with pure equanimity and awareness.
an10.20:10.3: That’s how a bhikkhu has stilled the physical process.
an10.20:11.1: And how is a bhikkhu well freed in mind?
an10.20:11.2: It’s when a bhikkhu’s mind is freed from greed, hate, and delusion.
an10.20:11.3: That’s how a bhikkhu is well freed in mind.
an10.20:12.1: And how is a bhikkhu well freed by wisdom?
an10.20:12.2: It’s when a bhikkhu understands: ‘I’ve given up greed, hate, and delusion, cut them off at the root, made them like a palm stump, obliterated them, so they’re unable to arise in the future.’
an10.20:12.3: That’s how a bhikkhu’s mind is well freed by wisdom.
an10.20:13.1: Bhikkhus, whether in the past, future, or present, all noble ones abide in these same ten abodes of the noble ones.
an10.20:13.4: These are the ten abodes of the noble ones in which the noble ones of the past, present, and future abide.”
